what_its_for: Temozolomide is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of brain tumors, including glioblastoma multiforme (a fast-growing brain tumor) and astrocytoma (another type of brain tumor). It works by stopping or slowing the growth of cancer cells.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Do not open, chew, crush, or break the capsules. Take temozolomide on an empty stomach or at bedtime to help reduce nausea. If a capsule is accidentally opened or broken, avoid breathing in the powder or letting it touch your skin. If contact occurs, wash the area right away with soap and water. Always wash your hands after handling the capsules.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your dose based on your body size (height and weight) and the type of brain tumor you have. Doses are usually taken once a day for 5 days in a row, then you have 23 days off — this makes one 28-day treatment cycle. In some cases, you may take it every day during radiation therapy. Never change your dose on your own. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store temozolomide capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed and out of reach of children and pets. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused or expired capsules — do not flush them down the toilet or throw them in the trash.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who are sick or have infections, as this medicine can weaken your immune system and make it harder to fight illness. Avoid live vaccines (such as flu nasal spray or chickenpox vaccine) while taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first. Avoid pregnancy — this medicine can seriously harm an unborn baby. Both men and women should use reliable birth control during treatment and for several months after. Do not breastfeed while taking temozolomide. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or tired.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, unusual bruising or bleeding, signs of infection (chills, sore throat, painful urination), severe nausea or vomiting that you cannot control, blood in your urine or stool, extreme tiredness or weakness, seizures, sudden changes in vision or speech, trouble walking or new numbness, signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing), or yellowing of your skin or eyes. Also tell your doctor about any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: Temozolomide does not work overnight. It may take several weeks or treatment cycles before your doctor can tell if the medicine is helping. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular blood tests and brain scans. It is important to keep all your follow-up appointments even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use temozolomide if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious birth defects or harm to the baby. Both men and women must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Children: This medicine can be used in children under close medical supervision, but dosing will be carefully calculated by the doctor based on the child's body size. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as low blood counts and fatigue. Close monitoring is important. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
